title: Spanish Cinema: Start Here
intro: Spain does two things better than almost anyone: melodrama that is unashamed of its own feelings, and thrillers with locks that click shut behind you. Almodóvar owns the first, a whole generation of Netflix hits owns the second, and Guillermo del Toro borrowed the country's ghosts for the best film he ever made.

films.title: Pan's Labyrinth
films.blurb: In 1944, a girl moves with her pregnant mother to the outpost of her new stepfather, a fascist captain, and finds a faun in a stone labyrinth who gives her three tasks. A fairy tale with real monsters on both sides of the frame. Not for children, despite the girl.

films.title: The Invisible Guest
films.blurb: A businessman wakes up in a locked hotel room next to his dead lover and has one night with a lawyer to build his defence. Every version of the story is a lie that fixes the last one. India adored this one, and remade it as Badla. Watch the original.

films.title: The Platform
films.blurb: A vertical prison where a feast descends one floor at a time, and the people at the bottom get what is left. One idea, pushed all the way. Grim, clever, and impossible to stop once it starts.

films.title: Society of the Snow
films.blurb: A rugby team's plane crashes in the Andes in 1972, and the survivors have seventy-two days of snow. The true story you may know, told with a tenderness that no earlier version managed. It is about who carries whom.

films.title: Talk to Her
films.blurb: Two men sit beside two women in comas, one a dancer and one a bullfighter, and a strange friendship grows in the hospital corridors. Almodóvar at his most controlled and most unsettling. It goes somewhere you will not expect and asks you to keep feeling.

films.title: Volver
films.blurb: Penélope Cruz plays a working mother in Madrid dealing with a body in the freezer, a village full of superstition, and her dead mother, who appears to be back. Warm, red, alive, full of women looking after each other. The friendliest way into Almodóvar.

films.title: Pain and Glory
films.blurb: An ageing film director in chronic pain drifts through memories of his mother, his first desire, and the actor he fell out with thirty years ago. Antonio Banderas plays a version of Almodóvar himself and has never been better. Quiet, autumnal, forgiving.

films.title: The Orphanage
films.blurb: A woman moves back into the orphanage she grew up in, planning to reopen it, and her young son starts talking to friends nobody can see. A ghost story with a mother's grief at its centre. The scares are real and the ending is worse.

films.title: The Sea Inside
films.blurb: Javier Bardem plays Ramón Sampedro, a man paralysed for nearly thirty years who fought the Spanish courts for the right to end his life. Based on a true story, and somehow full of humour and love. It won the Oscar for a reason.

films.title: The Skin I Live In
films.blurb: A plastic surgeon keeps a woman in a locked room in his mansion, testing a synthetic skin he has invented on her. The less you know, the better. Almodóvar's coldest and strangest film, and one you will want to talk about immediately.
